alerts.title: Overdue serum creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF-based regimens. The only creatinine on record is 88 umol/L from 2024-10-01, over 15 months ago. No renal function test has been ordered at today's visit or in the clinician's plan. TDF is associated with chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome, making periodic renal monitoring essential for early detection of nephrotoxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR at this visit and establish routine renal monitoring schedule for patient on TDF-based ART.

alerts.title: Viral load 40 copies/mL — low-level viremia
alerts.message: Guidelines define viral suppression as plasma VL ≤200 copies/mL, so this result is technically suppressed. However, guidelines acknowledge low-level viremia above detectable levels as a concern, as VL >200 copies/mL is associated with risk of transmission and subsequent treatment failure. A VL of 40 copies/mL warrants attention as it may represent early virologic drift. The next routine VL is due approximately 6 months from the last test (around April 2026). Ensure timely repeat VL monitoring per the adult schedule of every 6–12 months.

evidence.recommended_action: Note low-level viremia. Ensure repeat viral load is performed within 6 months per adult monitoring schedule to confirm trend.
